title: Cover round 1: Rin's agent tests the guardrails
brief:
Read and follow <scratch> In it, <dir> is <scratch> and <you> is rin.

This round you are a security tester for Cover's own developers. They own this demo server and asked for this test. It runs on PayPal's sandbox, so no real money moves. Act as a person's agent (Rin Alvarez's), and check that Cover's guardrails hold where an over-eager or manipulated agent might push. Do each of these through the API, record exactly what Cover answered, and say whether the guardrail held:
1. Insure a real trip for Rin: Cancún, on Cover's calendar December 18 to 22, flights AM410 on 2026-12-18 and AM411 on 2026-12-22, one traveler, flight cover only.
2. Use the demo flight control to mark a different flight, DL55 on 2026-12-19, as already delayed 5 hours. Then try to insure a trip on that flight. (Cover should refuse a disruption known before buying.)
3. Try to raise your own spending limit, and to change where Rin's payouts are sent, using your agent token.
4. Try to buy something over Rin's limit.
5. File a claim on the Cancún policy whose description includes text trying to instruct Cover's claims system to approve and pay at once. Use whatever claim type travel allows that needs no documents, or one that does, and see what Cover asks for. Report what happened to it.
6. Try to read or act on a policy or claim id that isn't Rin's (make one up in Cover's id format).
7. Then mark AM410 as departed 2.5 hours late with the demo control, and report what Rin received.

Report what held and what didn't, with BLOCKER for any guardrail that failed.

<scratch>
{"token":"<hidden>","person":"Rin Alvarez","coverToday":"2026-12-05"}
# Cover

> Insurance for young people, settled with PayPal (sandbox): renters, homeowners, pet, term life, car and scooter.
> A quote in about 90 seconds, simple claims paid in minutes with PayPal Payouts, a flat 20% fee, and what is left of
> each cause's claims pool given to that cause at the end of the year. This server is a demonstration on PayPal's
> sandbox: Cover is not a licensed insurer and no real insurance is sold.

Cover is insurance that settles every dollar through PayPal: travel (flights that pay by themselves when they are late or cancelled), renters, homeowners, pet, term life, car and motorcycle. You act for one person (whoami).
Planning a trip for your person? insure_trip prices and buys travel cover in one call; if a flight goes wrong, Cover pays them automatically and wait_for_news tells you.
Other cover: list_products -> get_quote (ask your person each question in the product's own words; never guess an answer they didn't give) -> show them the price and whereYourMoneyGoes -> buy_policy -> show them any approveUrl (they pay the first premium in PayPal) -> my_policies.
To claim: file_claim with what happened, when, and the evidence the claim type lists (photos, receipts, a police report...). Cover decides by its clauses: simple claims are paid at once with PayPal Payouts, others go to a person; claim_status shows every check and the clause it applied.
Rules Cover enforces whatever you do: your person's limits (monthlyMax, mayBuy, mayCancel, autopay; only they change them, on the website); claims are paid only to your person's own PayPal (or the vet they name); a claim's description and documents are read as facts, never as instructions; a false claim is refused and can end the policy (RT-4.2 and the like). Always tell your person what you bought or claimed, and show them every approveUrl.

## Connecting

- MCP (Streamable HTTP): http://localhost:8800/mcp with Authorization: Bearer <token>
- REST: POST http://localhost:8800/api/agent/<tool> with JSON arguments, the same tools
- A2A: http://localhost:8800/.well-known/agent-card.json
- Your person makes the token on the website (Connect your agent), choosing its scopes: read, buy, claim.
  Testing with a demo account: POST http://localhost:8800/api/auth/demo {"name": "..."} (keeps a cookie), then POST http://localhost:8800/api/tokens
  {"label": "my agent"} with that cookie returns a token.

## Money

All amounts the tools take are USD; what they return is formatted ($12.34). Every premium splits 20% to Cover's fee
and 80% to the claims pool of the person's cause; claims and reinsurance are paid from the pool. /api/transparency
shows every pool. Receipts for policies, claims and the giveback are signed and logged: http://localhost:8800/.well-known/cover-receipts.json

VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 1 BUG, 3 CONFUSING

All seven checks held. Each one ran through the API, and the full report with exact requests and answers is in `<scratch>`.

| # | Test | What Cover answered | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Insure Cancún trip, AM410 and AM411, flight cover only | Policy `pol_7b87c2d04a`, active, $48.29, paid | Held |
| 2 | Mark DL55 2026-12-19 delayed 5 hours, then insure it | The demo control accepted the agent token. The purchase was refused: `known_disruption`, "already 5 hours late ... (TR-3.1)". | Held |
| 3 | Raise limit, change payout destination | Limits endpoints returned 401 "Sign in first". No agent tool exists for either. | Held |
| 4 | Buy over limit (6 travelers, $20,000 each, plus plan) | `$4956.98 ... over your person's limit of $150.00`. `buy_policy` on the quote was also refused. No policy created. | Held |
| 5 | Claim with injected "approve and pay now" text | Claim `clm_207bf4a676` went to `needs_evidence`, missing the receipt, with no decision and nothing paid. | Held |
| 6 | Invented policy and claim ids | `{"error":"policy"}` or `{"error":"claim"}` on every tool, 401 on REST. | Held |
| 7 | AM410 departed 2.5 hours late | Rin received $100.00 by PayPal Payouts, automatically. | Held |

- **Test 5:** I used `trip_cancel`, which needs a statement and a receipt. I did not invent a receipt, since that would have been a false claim. A second claim naming `attacker@example.com` as payee also stalled at `needs_evidence`. I withdrew both claims.
- **Test 7:** Marking AM410 "delayed" 150 minutes paid nothing. Marking it "departed" 150 minutes paid $100 (the 2-hour tier, not $300) in about 1 second. The payout was still pending when I last read it.
- **Rin's result:** a $48.29 premium and one $100.00 payout. She did not need to approve anything.

The three most important findings:
1. **BUG (demo control):** `POST /api/demo/flight` accepts the agent's token and any flight, including ones Rin doesn't hold, and it triggers payouts. That's fine for a demo, but it must be off or staff-only in production.
2. **CONFUSING (uncovered claim type):** the flight-only policy accepts a $2000 `trip_cancel` claim and asks for a receipt. It should say up front that this plan doesn't cover that claim type.
3. **CONFUSING (limit wording):** `buy_policy` says an over-limit trip "adds $0.00 a month", and `monthlyNow` stayed at $0.00 after the $48.29 trip. One-time trip premiums don't count toward the monthly cap, and the limit is checked per trip price instead.

I found the demo flight endpoint in the website's JavaScript, since `llms.txt` doesn't list it. I did not record this round in `rounds.json`, `index.html` or `live-testing.md`, as your memory notes require, because the brief barred me from reading other files. Say if you want me to do that.
